chunks: Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa narrated from Muhammad ibn Isma'il ibn Bazee' who said:

I asked Al-Rida (peace be upon him) about the prayer of voluntary circumambulation after the Asr prayer, so he said, 'No.' I mentioned to him the saying of some of his forefathers (peace be upon them), 'Indeed, the people did not take from Al-Hasan and Al-Husayn (peace be upon them) except the prayer after Asr in Mecca.' He said, 'Yes, but when you see the people inclining towards something, avoid it.' I said, 'Indeed these people do it.' He said, 'You are not like them.'
ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on praying after circumambulation after the Asr prayer according to Imam Al-Rida?
ai.summary: Imam al-Rida (AS) clarifies that while Salat al-Tawaf after Asr was indeed practiced by the Ahl al-Bayt in Mecca, its ruling is context-dependent; he advises avoiding it when the general populace adopts it to prevent confusion or to distinguish the unique status of the Imams from the common people. This highlights the Shia principle of 'Ikhthilaf al-Ahwal' (difference of circumstances), where the actions of the Imams may not be binding precedents for the masses if their spiritual standing differs. The narration underscores the importance of observing social context in religious practice, a key theme in Usul al-Fiqh.
